items.title: ‘God Of War’ Kratos actor reveals why he didn’t return for TV show
items.summary: Christopher Judge was in “talks” to reprise his role
items.content:
Gaming News Original ‘God Of War’ Kratos actor reveals why he didn’t return for Amazon adaptation Christopher Judge was in “talks” to reprise his role

Kratos in ‘God Of War: Ragnarök’. CREDIT: Santa Monica Studios

Original God Of War Kratos actor Christopher Judge has explained why he didn’t reprise his role for the Amazon adaptation.

Christopher Judge played Kratos, the titular God Of War, in the 2018 reboot as well as 2022 sequel Ragnarok . However for the upcoming Amazon Prime Video adaptation Ryan Hurst, the actor behind game antagonist Thor, was set to take on the role of Kratos before an on-set injury forced him to step down . Now Dave Bautista is set to play Kratos in the God Of War live-action series.

Speaking at a panel over the weekend though, Judge revealed that he was in talks to return as Kratos before he ultimately decided to pass on the role. “We had talked and I thought, ‘God, what a great legacy to leave for my grandson.’ So I started working out. I got bigger,” he said (via IGN ).

“I did read for it [but] it was so hard for me to memorise my lines, which I never had a problem with [before]. And that was my mind and body starting to tell me, ‘You don’t want to do this.’ I was one of the leads of Stargate at 33 to 44, and then stopped. Now, at 62, to be the lead, I just have no desire to live that way again. I didn’t want to, at 62 years old, work 18-hour days. I didn’t want to be dieting constantly. I didn’t want to be working out constantly.”

The next God Of War game will launch next year and focus on Kratos’ dead wife Laufey as she journeys through the afterlife. After that, the series will return to Kratos’ story , though it’s not known if Judge will return for that. “While [God Of War: Laufey] is a different thing, it’s still part of the larger tapestry of what we truly want to explore [with] all these different characters in there,” explained studio boss Cory Barlog in an interview in June. “But there’s always going to be Kratos games throughout the whole history.”

In other news, Rockstar Games has announced the “next evolution” of the fan-created Roleplay spin-off game from Grand Theft Auto Online with nopixel 5 set to go live early next week for select players.

items.title: 10 Open World Games with Near-Perfect Scores
items.summary: While these games didn't get perfect scores, they scored close enough that they might as well have.
items.content:
By Elena Chapella Published Aug 29, 2026, 2:30 PM EDT Elena is a Contributing Writer at DualShockers specializing in horror games, survival horror, open-world RPGs, fantasy, and historical fiction. She began covering games professionally in 2024, with her early gaming focus tied to Baldur’s Gate 3 before her interest in horror coverage grew through games like Silent Hill 2 Remake and Silent Hill f .

on Google Preferred Source Google News Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Of course, it’s impossible to expect perfection from any work of art – and video games are no exception to this. That being said, that doesn’t mean that there aren’t open world games that come very, very close to perfection.

These open world games not only set a new standard, but they completely blew our current standards out of the water. It’s a rare instance where both audiences and critics alike shower the game in constant praise.

Some open world RPGs wanted to stand out from the rest, so they did.

We took a look at OpenCritic , our official review aggregating system, and found the top open world games with scores that teeter on perfection; these are games that, despite the odds of probability (as in there is bound to be someone who dislikes the game), earned applause from most, if not all the top critics.

And if you’ve played any of these games, you’d know exactly why they scored so impeccably.

Expand Collapse Just a moment of clarity and transparency before continuing: technically, Forza Horizon 5 has a higher OpenCritic score of 92, however, if you were to ask any critic or player who enjoys these games, everyone points to Forza Horizon 6 as the near-perfect one, especially with how it improves upon the previous entry. Since it scored a 91, a technical near-tie, we at DualShockers made the editorial decision to opt for FH6 instead, since it’s taking the community by storm.

When you think of an open world game, you don’t often think of them being a racing game as well, but that’s actually exactly what you get with Forza Horizon 6. You can just casually roam around Japan and soak in the country’s beauty, and if you find some sick races to do in the meantime, even better.

The open world feels more like a massive playground , especially since the game incorporates more platformer and collect-a-thon elements to make the world more dynamic. By the time you’re done with the races, you’re not even done with the game, you’re just going to want to drive around the world as fast as you can.

Forza Horizon 6 is truly a game that will surprise you, especially for a racing game, and once you have a chance to play it for yourself, you'll understand why we're going for this one over its predecessor.

God of War Ragnarok Action Adventure FX Wiki Wiki

Expand Collapse The modern God of War games are truly unlike anything fans of the Greek classics were accustomed to, but the series as a whole became so much stronger because of it. God of War Ragnarök , in particular, ended up becoming one of the most infamous games in the franchise, outpacing even the classics in sales and in praise.

It sits comfortably with a score of 92 on OpenCritic, showing how it was adored by players and reviewers alike, and it's not just because of the world itself. Sure, the Norse mythology is cool, and it runs like melted butter, but the main thing that it deserves all the love for is its impactful story and sick gameplay. Not to mention everyone's performance is outright cinematic.

It's a game that improved upon everything that players loved about the 2018 God of War, while also providing enough newness to keep everything exciting – and let me tell you, this game is constantly exciting. You're going to find yourself hyped about all kinds of things you'd never expect, and this is immediate with our first encounter with Thor.

Sign in to your Collider account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap The God of War franchise is about to enter a whole new world of deities next year with the release of its latest installment, God of War: Laufey . Acting as a parallel story to Kratos and Atreus' Norse journey in God of War 2018 and its sequel, Ragnarök , it'll mark a massive return for the series after five years, following the Ghost of Sparta's second wife, Faye, through the afterlife of the gods, where she will meet curious new allies and battle all-powerful beings from other pantheons, like the Egyptian goddess of war Sekhmet and the Mongolian lord of war, Begtse. Her ultimate goal is to protect her family after learning that her arrangements to keep Kratos and Atreus safe are in jeopardy. With Deborah Ann Woll 's fierce Jötnar getting the focus, it also means each member of Kratos' family has, in a way, had their own story in the modern era of the series.

God of War 2018 was very much Kratos' story of not just preparing his young son for the world, but learning from him how to be a better person and ultimately sharing with him his history as a killer of gods . While players still controlled the Spartan in Ragnarök , the sequel was more Atreus' tale , making him a playable character and following the duo initially in an effort to save the Nine Realms from the titular incoming disaster. He takes the lead for much of the adventure, coming into his own while Kratos supports him along the way, battling other Norse deities now that the Allfather Odin has them in his sights . The game ultimately brings the Norse saga to an end by sending the son on his own path to search for the surviving giants, but while his future is yet to be written, Prime 1 Studio is returning to his tale in style.

The premium collectible company is following up on its previous statues of Kratos and the god of thunder, Thor , with a stunning new piece commemorating the Ghost of Sparta 's son in all of his forms. Speculative Fiction Collectibles has opened pre-orders for a new statue based on Atreus' appearance in God of War Ragnarök , complete with swappable parts and flanked by his bear and wolf forms. It captures the teenager in extreme detail, showing his growth as a confident and capable warrior in his own right and acting as a monument to his journey, even handing him the Mask of Creation that Odin so desperately sought. This piece won't ship until 2028, but fans with plenty of cash to spare, specifically $3,099, can secure the limited-edition item for themselves now.

items.title: God of War Ragnarök is the best video game story in a decade — here’s why
items.summary: God of War Ragnarök is the rare sequel that actually sticks the landing — brutal combat, genuine emotional weight, and an ending that earns it.
items.content:
This post may contain affiliate links. For more information, please read our affiliate disclosure policy . TL;DR God of War Ragnarök is a brutally satisfying conclusion to Kratos and Atreus’s Norse saga. The combat is some of the best on PS5, the story has genuine emotional weight, and the ending actually feels earned. Play the 2018 reboot first — you’ll need it.

So I've spent a serious chunk of time with God of War Ragnarök and I have to tell you — it's the rare sequel that actually sticks the landing. Not 'pretty good for a sequel.' Actually sticks it.

This isn't just a video game. It's a brutal, gorgeous meditation on fathers and sons, redemption and ruin, told through the eyes of two characters you genuinely care about. And yeah, the combat is absolutely unhinged in the best way.

Santa Monica Studio could've coasted. They didn't.

Most games don't earn their conclusions — they just sort of… stop. Ragnarök is different. Every story beat, every quiet moment between Kratos and Atreus, every piece of Norse mythology woven into the world has been building toward this since the 2018 reboot. The prophecy. The fate of the Nine Realms. What Kratos is actually afraid of.

It all lands. Which is not something I say lightly.

I've written before about games that tried to do too much and ended up doing nothing — Ragnarök is the opposite problem. It does everything and somehow pulls it off.

Yes. Aggressively, almost offensively good. You've got the Leviathan Axe, the Blades of Chaos, and new moves that make every single fight feel fresh even forty hours in. The difficulty scaling actually works — there's a real sweet spot between "I'm just mashing buttons" and "I need to lie down."

The environmental kills alone are worth the price of admission. Finding new ways to smash a giant's face into a wall genuinely never gets old. But what do I know — I also think the Blades of Chaos sound design deserves some kind of award.

Does the story hit harder than the first game? Without spoiling anything — and I mean I genuinely won't — the writing in Ragnarök operates at a level most prestige TV can't reach. Atreus goes through real character development that doesn't feel forced. Mimir's voice acting will make you forget he's a disembodied head on your belt.

There's a scene about halfway through that made me pause and just sit there for a minute. Not because something exploded. Because something was said. That's rare in any medium, not just gaming.

Plan on 30 to 40 hours for the main story plus side quests. And the side content actually matters here — it's not fetch quests designed to pad a number. Some of the optional boss fights are harder than the main campaign bosses, and the rewards are worth chasing.

There's a full New Game+ mode too, if you somehow want to go back through it all with upgraded gear and a harder difficulty. Which, honestly, you probably will.

Your TV will feel inadequate. I played on a PS5 with a decent 4K setup and there were genuine moments where I just stopped moving to look at Midgard or Muspelheim. The level design is architectural perfection — every area tells a story just by existing in it.

items.title: God of War Laufey Releases Feb. 16, 2027; Next Kratos-Led Game Coming After It
items.summary: God of War Laufey releases February 16, 2027, as a new Kratos-led game is coming after it and ties to its story.
items.content:
Revealed two months ago , God of War Laufey is the latest game in the franchise, though one with a new protagonist. If you’re excited to play another entry in the series, you’ll be glad to know we don’t have to wait long to experience it.

Sony has announced that God of War Laufey will be released on PS5 on February 16, 2027!

Not only did we get that info today, but confirmation of the next game after it too.

At San Diego Comic Con (via IGN ), Cory Barlog, studio head of creative at Santa Monica Studio, announced that the next Kratos-led God of War game is coming after Laufey, and connects directly to her story.

No further details were shared, so we don’t know the release date/window, which pantheon the game will be set at, etc. That said, given we saw Kratos make an appearance in God of War Laufey’s reveal gameplay trailer, this is hardly surprising.

For those not caught up to the latest God of War game on the way, Sony explains Laufey’s storyline as:

“Death was supposed to be the end, but for Laufey (Faye), warrior and wife to Kratos, a new adventure is just beginning. Awakening unexpectedly in a strange land after her death, Faye discovers the plans she put in place to protect Kratos and Atreus in her absence are now at risk.

To save the ones she loves, Faye must fight through the afterlife of the gods – the Everywhen – where ruthless gods from across mythology vie for power in a land overflowing with dangerous magic.

Harness Faye’s speed, control and relentlessness to overwhelm even the fiercest of foes with decisive, deadly precision.”

Laufey isn’t really shown in God of War (2018), but she is a “Guardian of the Jötnar, rebel leader against the oppressive Aesir gods, and lone protector of the Wildwoods – Laufey is a warrior whose battle prowess was legendary even among the Giants.”

Expect Laufey to expand the God of War universe, and give the character a proper story since all we saw was her dead at the start of Kratos’ Norse journey.

With God of War Laufey releasing early next year, a God of War Greek mythology remake , and confirmation of a new Kratos-led God of War title coming after Laufey, franchise fans be eating good!

That said, given Laufey is releasing next year, don’t expect a disc-based version of Kratos’ upcoming adventure, since Sony is ceasing physical disc versions of new games at the start of January 2028 . Unless Santa Monica Studio releases two God of War games in a year, which we’re willing to bet money on that it won’t happen.

items.title: New Kratos-Led 'God of War' Game With Ties to Laufey on the Way
items.summary: A new 'God of War' game led by Kratos is in development, ...
items.content:
Comment Save Share Comments Comments YouTube/Playstation *:empty]:hidden"> Key Takeaways Santa Monica Studio used its SDCC 2026 panel "Forging God of War's Next Heroes" to confirm a new Kratos-led God of War game that will connect directly to the story of God of War: Laufey . God of War: Laufey makes Faye the series' first non-Kratos lead, following her in the afterlife realm Everywhen as she races to protect the plans she set for Kratos and Atreus while gods from multiple mythologies battle for power. Deborah Ann Woll calls Laufey a "reluctant hero," while Kratos actor Chris Judge says Faye is the "genesis" of Kratos' change toward hope, forgiveness, and being better, underscoring her importance to both the Norse saga and the next mainline game. A new God of War game led by Kratos is in development, and it will connect directly to the events of God of War: Laufey .

The franchise-shaking reveal was confirmed on Friday (July 24) by PlayStation's Santa Monica Studio during its San Diego Comic-Con panel, "Forging God of War's Next Heroes."

Elsewhere during the panel, Deborah Ann Wolf, who voices Laufey, Kratos' wife, in the upcoming God of War Laufey , described her character as a "reluctant hero."

Kratos’ voice actor, Chris Judge, also spoke about the importance of her character in both God of War and God of War: Ragnarok.

"I always thought that Faye was the genesis of the change of Kratos," he said. "So much of the message in the first two games was about hope and forgiveness and being better. I think that all started with Kratos' relationship with Faye. That's where it began in him and what kept him going was ensuring that this wonderful life that we had created together would be better than the old man."

God of War: Laufey is the first entry in the series where Kratos sits out as the primary playable character. The game follows Kratos's wife, who wakes in a mystical afterlife realm called the Everywhen after her funeral and races to protect the plans she put in motion for Kratos and their son, Atreus.

Judge returns to voice Kratos in a supporting capacity, with Jack Quaid voicing a companion named Phranque and Perlina Lau voicing ribbon-and-sword spirit Rue.

Laufey is set parallel to God of War (2018) and God of War Ragnarok , beginning in the immediate aftermath of Faye's death at the opening of the 2018 game. The Everywhen is described as the source of all magic in the universe, where beings from across mythologies fight for dominance.

items.title: New God of War game does not feature the god of war
items.summary: God of War is back, but this time minus the titular God of War. God of War: Laufey will instead focus on Kratos' dead wife Faye.
items.content:
Honestly, I wondered what game announcement could possibly be so hype-inducing that PlayStation would rent out theaters nationwide to host it. The Last of Us 3 ? Bloodborne 2 ? Unfortunately, the levels of hype weren't quite that nuclear, but the show's much-speculated-about 'one last thing' — a new God of War game from Santa Monica Studio — was still pretty nice to see.

With a caveat, of course. This is not a sequel to God of War: Ragnarok . Rather, it's a spinoff starring Faye , Kratos' Giant (but not giant) wife whose death kicked off the events of the 2018 reboot and its sequel. The clock is rewound to the moment of her cremation, setting the stage for a story that follows her through the gods' shared afterlife.

All the gods, not just the Norse ones, the modern saga has shown. The Egyptian Sekhmet looks to be the big bad, at least from what's been revealed so far, with the obscure Mongolian Begtse co-starring as her lieutenant. While I'm all the way on board for the multicultural pantheon-on-pantheon action, I'm less enthralled by the companion characters. I simply cannot care about a funny gelatinous cube named Frank in the same way as I did Kratos' son, Atreus. The tone looks, quite frankly, all over the place in a way that makes me a bit skeptical, but I'll be keeping an eye on this one all the same.

items.title: God of War Laufey Is Taking the Sort of Risk More PlayStation Series Need To Take
items.content: It may sport the series’ title, but Laufey isn’t your typical God of War game. Kratos is out, and Faye is in, taking up the protagonist's mantle. It’s the first time the series has shifted perspective in its 21 year lifetime, and doing so brings significant change. Not only will we be exploring a brand new world through the eyes of a different kind of hero, but Faye’s approach to battling her enemies is different to that of her gruff axe-and-blade wielding husband. Gone are the heavy slams and flesh-ripping finishers, replaced with magical sword swings and aerial juggling. It marks a reinvention, albeit one that still occurs within the familiar cinematic framework that has long been the foundation for Sony’s raft of third-person, cinematic action adventures. The PlayStation approach to single-player stories appeals to me in a way that other developer’s styles rarely do. But that doesn’t mean I haven’t been hoping for something a bit different. I’ve previously written about how I’m getting bored of every PlayStation game telling the same story , but in all honesty, it’s gone beyond familiar tales. Sony’s first-party games increasingly feel cut from the same cloth, their overall experiences overlapping. Sequels rarely diverge from the formula set out before them, feeling almost like full-length expansions rather than new iterations. This wasn’t too much of an issue when triple-A development cycles were much shorter and the space between Uncharted games, for example, was only a couple of years. But in an age where we’re looking at a good six to seven years between PlayStation Studios releases at best, I crave something altogether fresher each time. The most recent State of Play gave me hope, though, with the reveal of God of War Laufey leading that charge. My personal fatigue is perhaps best exemplified by last year’s Ghost of Yotei, Sucker Punch’s sequel to Ghost of Tsushima. Don’t get me wrong, it’s a game I mostly enjoyed playing to completion, but I was left wanting more. The original game’s formula was a fantastic riff on the samurai fantasy in a post-Assassin’s Creed world, so I can see why the studio would hesitate to deviate from the path. But doing it all over again with a different backdrop in Yotei just felt too familiar to ever become genuinely exciting. Atsu and Jin may be two distinctly different characters with their own personalities and traumas to battle through, but when it comes to controlling them through their violent journeys, they are mechanically largely identical. While combat may be slick, there’s limited variation between their approaches. More like this With GTA 6 Looming Over the Horizon, Sony Says It Has Secured Enough Memory to Meet Its PS5 Sales Targets This doesn’t look like it will be a problem for God of War Laufey, which is taking the bold step of replacing series icon Kratos with his Faye, his wife and mother to Atreus. Already dead before the opening of the Norse duology, Laufey is set to follow her journey through the afterlife, and looks filled with the sort of spectacle and layered storytelling we’ve come to expect from Santa Monica Studio. But what caught my eye most during the recent 20 minutes of gameplay showcased as part of State of Play is just how distinct Faye appears in combat. Look, I’m sure we’ll still be able to push both sticks in and erupt into a burst of violence just like you can in God of War. And Ghost of Yotei. And Saros. And Marvel’s Spider-Man. But her agile, faster-paced action looks so much more than Kratos reskinned, with her weapon packing personality into each slash and swing — quite literally, since the sword (or rather, the ribbon flowing from its hilt) speaks.

items.title: Gaming Respawn Plays (March 2026)
items.summary: At last, March is upon us, and with it some newer big games. But how many of us Gaming Respawners are playing these new, big games? Not a lot, apparently, except a couple of people. In fact, I know a couple of us have played Resident Evil Requiem, but strangely,...
items.content:
At last, March is upon us, and with it some newer big games. But how many of us Gaming Respawners are playing these new, big games? Not a lot, apparently, except a couple of people. In fact, I know a couple of us have played Resident Evil Requiem , but strangely, no mention of that game here. Instead, many of us are still experiencing “blasts from the past” and playing older titles going as far back as the PS2 era. Nothing wrong with that, it was a kickass era in gaming. Join us to see what we’ve all been playing lately in Gaming Respawn Plays (March 2026).

Got to say, I’m still in a bit of a funk, game-wise. God of War: Sons of Sparta should have been the game that dropped out of nowhere to take over my soul until I’d not only completed the game but got the platinum too.

The trouble is, that game is so bland, so safe, so uninspiring, so ‘meh’, I’ve not only stopped, I already deleted the game. How they can make a game so substandard for the God of War universe is beyond me, but somehow, they did it. It staggers me that Santa Monica Studio signed off on the final product too.

There is nothing inherently wrong with placing a young Kratos in a 2D Metroidvania-style game with pixel art, but the game is so devoid of fun or an interesting story that it’s just not worth the effort. I mean, it’s not until about ten hours in that you get something as simple as a double jump ability, for crying out loud.

So, to cheer myself up, I started playing an OG Kratos game again. I realised that the God of War: Ragnarok game I’d platinumed only had one playthrough, so I started playing that again. When playing a game for the second time, I always enjoy it a little more as I understand the story better and pick up on things I missed the first time.

November of this year will mark this game’s FOURTH anniversary! It’s bittersweet playing this again as I find it hard to think that here I am playing such a gorgeous, well-crafted and now old game again, simply because nothing else currently really tickles my fancy.

I’ve still got games like Cyberpunk 2077, Final Fantasy XVI , Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora , Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , and Hogwarts Legacy , amongst others, sitting on my shelf in my backlog of shame, either untouched or unfinished, and I just haven’t got the heart to put them on. I’ve also recently bought Black Myth: Wukong and Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden to now add to this stack.

I think the reason I’m drawn back to Ragnarok , though, is because I’ve spent three years trying to find the next big franchise to take my mind off God of War , and in that time, only Stellar Blade , Astro Bot , Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine II , and Battlefield 6 have managed to keep my interest for any length of time.

So, after feeling a little empty and annoyed, and to help me find my mojo again, I’ve had to press the reset button and play God of War: Ragnarok again to remind myself just how flipping good not just this series is but also games in general as a whole.

I am trying to get back into Ghost of Yotei now that it’s had an update, but I’m nervous to play it because of the console-stopping moments it’s given me.

Because of that, I’ve spent a lot of time opening up my PS5 to clean it as best I can without taking much out. To be fair, even though I’d not cleaned my console for about 6 months, there was hardly any dust in there. The worry now is, especially with playing Ghost of Yotei , is my console shutting down while playing because the liquid metal used to disperse the heat from the CPU to the heat sink is now oxidized.

If that is happening, the heat isn’t being dispersed as well as it should, even though the console is clean? I have a day one PS5, quite literally, and I do thrash my PS5 every day, one way or another, with games or media, so it may be this. I hope not, and I don’t think it really is as it’s only Ghost of Yotei and Battlefield 6 that I have this problem with. Both games have reported issues shutting down or freezing consoles. I’ve got 750 hours on Gran Turismo 7 , 250 hours on Space Marine II , and it’s never happened while playing those games. So, playing a game like God of War: Ragnarok is also testing the console as I never had an issue in the 85 hours it took me to play that game, so I hope I don’t have this issue the second time through either.

The OTHER big thing that is messing with my gaming disappointment is that March 2026 is the month that I was hoping to (but now won’t) play the only game I am truly stoked to play this year: 007 First Light . The initial release date was going to be the 27th March, but it’s now been pushed back to May.

A lot of my current trend of “treading water” with gaming, I think, is also trying to buy some time with something other than Battlefield 6 multiplayer until the Bond game arrives.

items.title: God Of War Sons Of Sparta (PlayStation 5) - Review
Why Amazon Seems To Be Skipping ‘God Of War’ For ‘Ragnarok’ In Its New Show
God of War Ragnarok's Free Update Adds Long Awaited Feature
items.summary: God of War Ragnarök has dropped a surprise free update for PlayStation 5 gamers.
items.content:
Prime Video’s God of War TV adaptation may have found its Kratos, but it’s not the only surprise in store for fans of Santa Monica Studio’s acclaimed franchise today.

God of War Ragnarök has just dropped a surprise new update that introduces a brand new feature that many of us will find incredibly useful.

As reported by PlayStation Lifestyle, update 06.06 has arrived for God of War Ragnarök and it “adds compatibility for Power Saver mode on PS5 and PS5 Pro”.

You may be thinking, “Is that it?”, but don’t underestimate the power of Power Save mode, my friends.

Power Save was first introduced to PlayStation 5 consoles in September of last year and it essentially reduces your console’s power consumption whilst playing games. Less power consumed is, first of all, great for the environment but perhaps more noticeably, it’s great for your bank account.

Reducing your power consumption whilst gaming will hopefully reduce your energy bills somewhat.

In the months since Power Save was introduced, we’ve seen various titles updated to support the feature and now, at long last, God of War Ragnarök joins the line-up.

That is all the update appears to do but we can hardly complain. It’s already been a major 24 hours for God of War fans.

In case you missed it, Ryan Hurst has been cast in the role of Kratos for Prime Video’s upcoming TV adaptation of God of War which, yes, will be live-action.

Hurst is already closely linked to the franchise having portrayed Thor in God of War Ragnarök , so it’ll be incredibly weird to now see him step into another role.

That does mean he’s already good buddies with video game Kratos actor Christopher Judge, so I wonder if Judge has already offered any words of advice.

Currently, Kratos is the only role that has been cast. There’s no word on who might portray Atreus, Sindri, Brok, Freya or Mimir.

By all accounts though, Hurst’s casting appears to have gone down well with fans which is a relief given that his name hadn’t really surfaced as an obvious fan pick.

The show is reportedly set to begin filming in March of this year, so I’d say we’re very likely looking at a 2027 premiere if all goes to plan.

items.content:
As a gift to everyone who owns God of War Ragnarök, the Dark Odyssey collection is now available in-game at no additional cost! Inspired by the working name of God of War (2005) and the skin that originally appeared in God of War II as a reward for beating the game on God Mode difficulty, we have brought back the black and gold theme for the anniversary.

Dark Odyssey Collection

Dark Odyssey Armor & Appearance for Kratos
  • Dark Odyssey Kratos Appearance
  • Dark Odyssey Armor Set for Kratos (Dark Odyssey Breastplate, Dark Odyssey Bracers, Dark Odyssey Belt)
Dark Odyssey Companion Armor
  • Dark Odyssey Vestment for Atreus
  • Dark Odyssey Witch Frock for Freya
Dark Odyssey Weapon Appearances & Attachments*
  • Dark Odyssey Leviathan Axe & Dark Odyssey Knob
  • Dark Odyssey Blades of Chaos & Dark Odyssey Handles
  • Dark Odyssey Draupnir Spear & Dark Odyssey Hind
Dark Odyssey Shield Appearances & Rönd
  • Dark Odyssey Guardian Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Dauntless Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Stone Wall Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Shatter Start Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Onslaught Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Spartan Aspis Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Rönd
*Please note, the weapon appearances are made for the fully upgraded version of each weapon and will only be available for use upon reaching that upgrade.

Edit Appearance for Weapon & Shield Attachments

With the addition of the new Dark Odyssey weapon attachments and shield rönd in the patch, we have added the ability to use the ‘Edit Appearance’ feature on those components of Kratos’ arsenal. You’ll be able to pick whatever visual suits your look with the functionality you want for your build!
